documents.title: EG for 2-connected bounded-degree δ≥3 expanders (conditional)
documents.label: CONJECTURAL
documents.summary: Every sufficiently large 2-connected α-expander with 3 ≤ δ ≤ Δ(G) ≤ Δ contains cycles of every even length in a linear range, in particular a cycle whose length is a power of two; and cycles of all residues mod every odd k (answering the bounded-degree case of Martinsson–Steiner's question).

documents.title: Induced cycles are ±1/±2 length adjusters when δ ≥ 3
documents.label: PROVED
documents.summary: If δ(G) ≥ 3 and Q is an induced cycle, any two vertices of Q have edges leaving Q; entering and leaving Q at two vertices at arc distance ⌊(q−1)/2⌋ gives two routes whose lengths differ by 1 or 2.

documents.title: 2-separated pockets and every edge give lengths differing by 1 or 2 (from Fan 2002)
documents.label: PROVED
documents.summary: If δ(G) ≥ 3 and (A,B) is a separation with A∩B = {u,v} and (G[B],u,v) rooted 2-connected, then any cycle through B can be rerouted inside B to change its length by 1 or 2. In a 2-connected δ≥3 graph every edge lies on two cycles whose lengths differ by 1 or 2.

documents.title: EG ⟺ f(k) ≥ 2^(k+1) for all k
documents.label: PROVED
documents.summary: Let f(k) be the minimum order of a graph with δ ≥ 3 and no cycle of length 2^2,…,2^k. Then the Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture holds iff f(k) ≥ 2^(k+1) for every k ≥ 2.

documents.summary: The Coxeter graph (28 vertices) has exactly 21 distinct 8-cycles and 609 distinct 16-cycles; the minimum vertex transversal of its 8-cycles has size 6 and that of its 16-cycles has size 5.

documents.title: Rooted robustness glues across nontrivial 3-edge cuts
documents.label: PROVED
